hints.content:
$g$ is decreasing in an interval where as $x$ increases, $g(x)$ decreases.

Visually, this is where the graph is going downwards as we go from left to right.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x-axis scales by one, and the y-axis scales by ten. The graph of y equals g of x is a continuous curve. From left to right, it passes through the point negative five, negative forty and the x-intercept negative four and one-half, zero. It continues to increase until the local maximum at negative three and one-half, twenty-eight. Then it decreases through to point negative three, twenty and the x-intercept negative two and one-quarter, zero until it reaches the local minimum at negative one, negative twenty. Then it increases through the origin and the point one, forty-five. It continues to increase until the local maximum two and one-half, ninety. Then it decreases through the point three, seventy and the x-intercept three and one-half, zero. All values are estimates. The function is highlighted from x equals negative three and one-half to x equals negative one and after x equals two and one-half.

hints.content:
Now we can check each option:

Interval | Is $g$ decreasing on the interval?
:-: | :-:
$-4.5<x<-4$ | $\redD{\text{No}}$. $g$ is increasing on this interval
$-3<x<-2$ | $\greenD{\text{Yes!}}$
$3<x<3.5$ | $\greenD{\text{Yes!}}$
